label: Bible Study
prompt: And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy _____ as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.
verse: And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.
note: The second great commandment — Jesus pairs it with loving God and says none is greater.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: _____ ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.
verse: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.
note: Isaiah turns from judgment to hope with a double 'comfort ye' — the first words sung in Handel's Messiah.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And the three companies blew the trumpets, and brake the _____, and held the lamps in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands to blow withal: and they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.
verse: And the three companies blew the trumpets, and brake the pitchers, and held the lamps in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands to blow withal: and they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.
note: Gideon's 300 went to battle with trumpets, lamps, and breakable pitchers — the strangest arsenal in Israel's history.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy _____ love.
verse: Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love.
note: Ephesus had sound doctrine, hard work and patience — and had quietly misplaced the love that started it all.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And the vessel that he made of clay was _____ in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
verse: And the vessel that he made of clay was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
note: At the potter's house the vessel was 'marred,' so he made it again — the second-chance sermon in clay.
